children: China's 2026 economic growth forecast remains intact, but growth will likely slow in the medium term, BofA Securities says in a research note. BofA keeps its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 4.5% in view of remaining policy room and policymakers' strong will to meet the growth target this year, the bank says. "Despite flashing red lights in domestic demand, supply side production will likely decelerate only gradually, limiting the extent of growth deceleration in the near future," they note. However, the bank expects the Chinese economy's growth to slow to 4.2% in 2027 and 4.0% in 2028. This is mainly due to headwinds for domestic activities and delayed policy easing, BofA says. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
